data.title: Tesla Rated Hold as Strong Auto Performance Offsets Volatile Energy Storage; $400 Price Target Reaffirmed
data.description:
Analyst Andrew Percoco from Morgan Stanley maintained a Hold rating on Tesla and keeping the price target at $400.00.

Andrew Percoco has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, balancing strong operating performance with valuation and execution risks. Tesla’s third-quarter auto deliveries significantly exceeded both his estimates and broader Street expectations, demonstrating resilient demand supported by rising fuel prices and continued improvements in the company’s autonomous driving capabilities. However, he notes that energy storage deployments, while near record levels, fell short of forecasts and remain inherently volatile on a quarterly basis, reinforcing the need to focus on longer-term trends rather than single-quarter prints.

Percoco’s stance reflects recognition of Tesla’s robust positioning in autos and energy, but also an awareness that the shares already price in much of this strength, limiting near-term upside from current levels. He expects demand for utility-scale energy storage and data center applications to remain healthy, yet sees the mixed momentum between segments as justifying a more balanced risk-reward view at this stage. As a result, he maintains a Hold recommendation on TSLA and leaves his price target unchanged at $400, indicating a view that the stock is fairly valued relative to its fundamental outlook and execution trajectory.

data.title: Regulatory Risks at Prudential Japan Sustain Sell Rating; Price Target Reaffirmed at $105
data.description:
Bob Huang, an analyst from Morgan Stanley, maintained the Sell rating on Prudential Financial. The associated price target remains the same with $105.00.

Bob Huang has given his Sell rating due to a combination of factors tied primarily to regulatory and operational risks in Prudential’s Japanese business. He views the potential formal sales suspension by the Japan FSA, along with a business improvement order for Prudential’s local holding company, as extending an already significant disruption to the franchise and adding further uncertainty to earnings visibility.

Huang believes that a longer suspension period, possibly stretching into late 2026 or early 2027, would keep the previously signaled 2026 hit of roughly $525–575 million in place and likely increase the expected $400–450 million impact for 2027. Given management’s indication that it may take 12–18 months for sales to fully recover after the suspension ends, he expects Prudential Japan’s operations to remain pressured well beyond the formal suspension, limiting near- to medium-term growth and supporting a Sell stance despite the unchanged $105 price target.

data.description:

Andrew Percoco has given his Sell rating due to a combination of factors related to Rivian’s long‑term execution risk and valuation versus its fundamentals. While the company delivered and produced materially more vehicles than expected in 3Q26 and kept its full‑year delivery guidance intact, he views the sustainability and mix of this strength as critical, particularly around the ramp of the R2 platform.

Percoco is concerned that if recent upside is driven mainly by R1 and EDV volumes, uncertainty around R2 scaling, profitability, and cash needs could continue to weigh on the equity story despite near‑term operational beats.
